title: Petra and the Harbor
premise: In the waning months of a naval war, Paloma Kavanagh keeps a secret ledger of soldiers whose deaths officers have erased from official reports. When a sealed letter from a dying quartermaster names her family in a supply-fraud conspiracy that cost hundreds of lives, Paloma must smuggle her ledger and the letter to a neutral harbor before the victors' historians seal the archives forever. Betrayed by the loyal friend she trusted most, she chooses truth over safety, testifying at an improvised tribunal aboard a decommissioned ship. The book ends with the record published and her brother's name restored — though Paloma herself must vanish into the harbor crowds, remembered only in the pages she saved.
about_author: Ulyana Okafor is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing war records across three continents. Petra and the Harbor is their second novel, inspired by the marginalia found in declassified field hospitals.

chapters.title: The Ledger Under the Floorboard
chapters.summary: Paloma Kavanagh, a battlefield nurse at a coastal garrison hospital, records in a hidden ledger the names of dead soldiers omitted from official reports. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: quiet defiance — she measures her days in what can be carried when evacuation orders come.

chapters.title: What the Officers Omit
chapters.summary: Paloma notices a pattern: every omitted name traces back to shipments logged by the same quartermaster, Elias Brandt. A surgeon warns her that asking questions gets nurses reassigned. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: unease hardening into resolve as she copies shipping numbers into her ledger.

chapters.title: A Letter Sealed in Wax
chapters.summary: Brandt, dying of fever, presses a sealed letter into Paloma's hands, whispering that it names 'the Kavanaghs' in a scheme that swapped medicine for ballast. He dies before explaining. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: dread — her family's name inside a plot no one wants a part of.

chapters.title: The Family in the Middle
chapters.summary: Paloma travels home on leave and confronts her uncle Tomas, a port official, who admits he signed manifests under threat. Her brother Devlin refuses to believe their name is tainted. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: loyalty strained as family closes ranks around silence.

chapters.title: Orders Come
chapters.summary: Evacuation orders reach the garrison; the army will burn its field records. Paloma realizes the ledger and Brandt's letter are all that will survive. She packs them among bandages. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: urgency — measuring the world again in what can be carried.

chapters.title: The Friend Who Stays
chapters.summary: Corporal Ada Reyes, Paloma's closest friend, offers to help carry the documents to the neutral harbor city of Petra. But Ada asks too many questions about the letter's seal. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: warmth shadowed by the first flicker of doubt.

chapters.title: Road to Petra
chapters.summary: The two women travel with a refugee column, hiding the ledger in a bread tin. At a checkpoint, an intelligence officer named Colonel Vasseur searches carts but misses the tin. POV: alternating Paloma/Ada. Emotional beat: terror and the intimacy of shared danger.

chapters.title: Harbor of Second Chances
chapters.summary: They reach Petra, a fog-bound neutral port full of deserters, printers, and victors' historians already arriving to write the official war. Paloma finds a sympathetic printer, Marek Sol. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: fragile hope — the truth might yet be printed.

chapters.title: The Historians' Archive
chapters.summary: Paloma infiltrates a reception where Vasseur oversees the sealing of wartime archives. She learns the fraud investigation will be closed as 'inconclusive' within weeks. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: cold clarity about how history is manufactured.

chapters.title: Devlin Arrives
chapters.summary: Her brother Devlin reaches Petra begging her to burn the letter — their uncle has been arrested, and cooperation could save him. Paloma refuses: the arrest proves the cover-up is accelerating. POV: Devlin. Emotional beat: love weaponized against truth.

chapters.title: Ada's Bargain
chapters.summary: Revealed: Ada has been reporting to Vasseur since the checkpoint, trading information for her imprisoned sister's release. She confesses to Paloma but begs one more day before turning over the ledger. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: guilt tearing loyalty apart.

chapters.title: The Tin Goes Missing
chapters.summary: Paloma wakes to find the bread tin gone. She suspects Ada; Ada swears Vasseur took it during the night raid. With the ledger lost, only Brandt's letter remains hidden in Paloma's boot. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: betrayal's vertigo — trust and evidence both gone.

chapters.title: Marek's Press
chapters.summary: Printer Marek Sol proposes an improvised tribunal: publish the letter alongside sworn testimony from witnesses gathering in Petra's taverns. Paloma must find witnesses faster than Vasseur can silence them. POV: Marek. Emotional beat: defiant invention — justice outside the law.

chapters.title: Witnesses in Taverns
chapters.summary: Paloma tracks down three survivors of the poisoned-supply convoy, including a mute gunner who can write his testimony. One witness disappears mid-interview; Vasseur's men are close. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: grim determination sharpened by grief.

chapters.title: Vasseur's Offer
chapters.summary: Colonel Vasseur meets Paloma privately: surrender the letter, and her uncle walks free and her brother is protected. He calls her ledger 'sentiment.' POV: Vasseur. Emotional beat: temptation framed as mercy — the system offering absolution for silence.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Weighs
chapters.summary: Paloma nearly accepts. Then she reads her ledger aloud to Devlin, name by name, until he stops arguing. Ada returns, having stolen the tin back from Vasseur's office at terrible risk. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: the turn — loyalty redefined as fidelity to the dead.

chapters.title: Night Before the Tribunal
chapters.summary: The witnesses gather aboard the decommissioned ship Meridian; Marek sets type by lamplight. Vasseur petitions the harbor authority to shut the proceedings down at dawn. POV: Ada. Emotional beat: hushed courage, everyone measuring what they're willing to lose.

chapters.title: Tribunal on the Meridian
chapters.summary: Testimony unfolds on the ship's deck: the gunner writes, survivors speak, Paloma reads the ledger's names aloud as the letter is entered into the record. Harbor crowds gather on the docks to listen. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: climax — the truth spoken publicly, unstoppable now.

chapters.title: The Victor's Historians
chapters.summary: Vasseur arrives with marines, but the crowd and two foreign journalists make seizure impossible. He pivots, claiming credit for exposing 'isolated corruption,' saving face while the record stands. POV: Marek. Emotional beat: bitter victory — justice done, but the powerful adapt.

chapters.title: Names Restored
chapters.summary: The broadsheet prints: the ledger, the letter, the testimony. Devlin wires word that their uncle will be released; the omitted soldiers' families begin receiving letters. POV: Devlin. Emotional beat: catharsis — grief given shape and acknowledgment.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Vasseur, humiliated but untouchable, moves to arrest Paloma on old charges. Ada and Marek arrange her escape on a fishing boat leaving with the morning tide. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: farewell — she leaves the ledger with Marek's archive, carrying only the memory of the names.

chapters.title: Petra and the Harbor
chapters.summary: Years later, a historian cites 'the Kavanagh papers' without knowing their keeper. In a distant town, Paloma nurses patients under another name, hearing her brother's name read aloud in a memorial. POV: Paloma. Emotional beat: resolution — the record outlived her, and that was enough.
